title: Add  Privacy Policy information
body:
In order to satisfy [requirements](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#legal) from Apple App store we need to add Privacy Policy window.
Suggestion is to have it in menu _Help_ ->  _Privacy Policy_
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
As I was thinking more on these recently, what about something we do more obvious to make the user aware of the newly introduced privacy policy? Something like opening with a window when Moonshine next time start with v1.16.0, describing with the privacy policy and force the user to agree to enter Moonshine. We can keep a flag to cookie to not to shown up the window again when next time Moonshine starts (if once agreed by the user).

I see a few advantage of this system:

1. User surely be aware of the newly introduce privacy policy by Moonshine
2. User will bound to be align with the privacy policy proposed (they never able to say we were not agreed at any circumstances)
3. We can use the same window system 'if' at sometime we require to update/change the privacy policy 

In my opinion, user will not be able to use the system if not accept by the terms, so that we can be assure by the new privacy policy laws enforced by the Apple/EU.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
I did some work drafting a privacy policy, but I realized that the SVN or Git credentials could be considered personal information.  I reviewed #307, and I think we can make the following assertions about how we use the credentials:
- Moonshine itself does not save the credentials
- The credentials will be passed to user-configured third-party applications.  These applications may save the credentials.
- The user is not required to enter credentials - they can save the credentials with the third-party application directly, or they can use an external source control application.

@rat-moonshine, please verify whether the code is consistent with these assertions.

Another case that I considered was the "This is great!" and "I'm having some problems" interfaces.   However, these interfaces do not request any personal information or account information from the user - instead the requests are forwarded to the Twitter, Facebook, or GitHub websites.  So, I don't think this needs any special attention in the privacy policy.

If anyone else thinks of other collected data that may need to be considered for the privacy policy,please let me know.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
I have checked through SVN and Git process on using the credentials, I confirm Moonshine do not stores any credential data to its local storage or neither to any server. While in case of Git, Moonshine provides option to re-use entered credential for the same application session - the entered credential stores to the memory as long Moonshine session is running, but I think this is irrelevant to an extent too. 

The Git authentication window is suppose to come if user do not have any credential already stored to the system keychain. It seems like once any Git command _push_ command executes with a credential, it stores to the keychain, and next time you don't even need to provide any credential. I seen the behaviour in Windows, too.

The bottom-line is, by executing any SVN or Git command with given credential through Moonshine, the credential may store to the system keychain (by SVN/Git application) but Moonshine has no control over it.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
> 
> 
> @JoelProminic , @JustinProminic - I have added privacy policy to Moonshine - it's under menu **Help** -> **Privacy Policy**. However I have one issue. I loaded privacy policy from HTML, because it's the easiest way of displaying it and have looking as it is in document.
> In order to load that html I used class called [FlexHTMLLoader](https://flex.apache.org/asdoc/mx/core/FlexHTMLLoader.html). In order to display what's is loaded I need to use UIComponent class, FlexHTMLLoader cannot be added to spark components. Unfortunately UIComponent doesn't have scrollbar, so I need to work a bit more in order to add those to displayed html. Currently you can scroll all content by mouse, but scrollbar is not visible.
> We can move slowly forward with release - I will try to work on that tomorrow more.

Please ensure the API do not use HTML API in-background. We can not bundle WebKit to the App Store version, they'll reject it.

On the other hand as an alternative, we can display the texts in-Moonshine as plain texts to an editor/tab and make it uneditable. 

[Edit: I noticed the link does navigates to browser later, instead of using Webkit]
